the turmeric supplementation to the broiler diet at level of 0.5 g/kg diet can be recommended as a phytogenic feed additive for broilers.

the use of turmeric as a phytogenic feed additive in broiler diets to enhance growth performance, carcass traits, and bacterial count.
the use of turmeric (C. longa) in broiler chickens as a phytogenetic feed additive to reduce the use of synthetic antibiotics in the broiler production.
the use of turmeric as a phytogenic growth promoter in broilers.

the turmeric supplementation at level 5 g/kg could be used as an alternative to antibiotics growth promoters in broiler chicken production.
, the use of 0.5 % turmeric powder as a growth promoter in broiler diets is a good choice.
turmeric powder could be used as a phytogenic feed additive for poultry.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, the turmeric supplementation at level of 500 mg/kg diet is recommended for broiler chickens as a phytobiotic to improve their growth performance and bacterial count.
, turmeric supplementation at level of 0.25%, 0.50% and 1.0% could be recommended for broiler production as a phytogenic additive to enhance the productive performance and bacterial counts.
, turmeric powder supplementation at level of 0.5 g/kg of feed could be considered a good alternative to antibiotic growth promoters in broilers diets.
The main takeaway from our work is that
turmeric supplementation can be used in poultry diets as an alternative to antibiotics.
turmeric is a safe and effective phytobiotic that can be added to poultry diets at a level of 0.5%.
the use of turmeric as a phytogenic growth promoter in broiler chicken diets can improve the performance of broiler chickens and reduce bacterial count.
